reason: The only available action is to use the auger at the ice, which seems like the first step toward supplying the water processor.
expectation: I expect the auger to extract ice or water that can be brought to the processor, though I don't know what form it will take.

effect: The auger created a heated well that brings untreated water to the surface, so the next step is to connect it for transport.
reaction: The warm probe producing a cloudy trickle makes the extraction process clear and leaves me curious about treatment.
reason: The hose is the only numbered option and seems suited to carrying water from the well toward the processor.
expectation: I expect the hose to connect to the well, possibly bringing the water to the processor; the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The hose now connects the heated well to the processor, and the strainer removes visible grit before the downstream treatment and checks.
reaction: The heated jacket and strainer make the water transport feel more concrete; I’m curious how the water will be made safe.
reason: The connected line is the only numbered action, and using it at the processor seems like the next step toward potable water.
expectation: I expect the processor to treat the raw water, though I don’t know whether that will complete the drinking-water checks.

effect: The processor removed suspended grit and dissolved contaminants, then checked the output before opening the tap. That completes the potable-water goal and clarifies the treatment sequence.
reaction: The almost tasteless first cup is a satisfying payoff for tracing the water from the ice bank to the tap.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using the connected well line at the processor was most worthwhile: it completed the water supply and explained the treatment and output check.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the hose was useful, but the single available action made the decision predictable.

surprise.text: I was interested that the extraction probe warms the buried ice and that the hose has a powered heating jacket.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary; each had a clear purpose in getting water from the ice to the tap.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because I enjoyed learning how the water system works and am curious about the expedition's next challenge, although this chapter offered little choice.
